newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W. Europe air passengers up 9.5 pct yr/yr in March.
newsitem.headline: W. Europe air passengers up 9.5 pct yr/yr in March.

text.p: Passenger traffic on major European airlines grew 9.5 percent year-on-year in March, the Association of European Airlines (AEA) said on Monday.
"Strong traffic growth was reported in March for the members of the Association of European Airlines," the industry association said in a statement.

"Part of the growth could be attributed to the Easter holiday weekend, which fell at the end of March this year but was in April the year before," said AEA, whose 26 members include all of the region's major scheduled carriers.
Of the three main operating regions, the highest growth was on the North Atlantic, up by 11.7 percent, followed by Europe with growth of 8.2 percent and the Far East at eight percent.
For the January-March period, passenger traffic rose 10.2 percent compared to the same period last year.

Aircraft load factors, measures of the seat take-up by fare-paying passengers, also improved in March year-on-year as capacity increase was less than traffic growth in all regions. It rose 1.3 percentage points to 74.6 percent.
"Highlights were an 81.1 percent load factor on the North Atlantic -- a truly remarkable figure for a period outside the high season -- and 63.8 percent in Europe," AEA said.

"While this latter figure is much more modest in comparison to the long-haul routes, it is nevertheless the highest March figure for Europe on record -- the first time a new monthly high has been posted in Europe since mid-1990," it added.
